text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government warns public service unions against staging planned nationwide strikes for increased wages, saying the consequences of their action would be negative.
- Commerce, trade and industry minister Alf Hambayi says the government will not allow investors to subject workers to slave wages in planned export processing zones.
- Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines says it is negotiating with the Zambia Revenue Authority to find better ways of paying its taxes without inconveniencing either itself or the authority.
- A Zimbabwean driver dies in a road accident involving six trucks in northern Zambia.
- Opposition leaders slam donors for ignoring government corruption in pledging to resume balance of payment support to the country at a Consultative Group meeting early this month.
